coordinates: pixels in the full scan above, origin top left
method: Each lateral frame cropped from the full scan at 0.6-0.75x (whole bird), 1.2x (legs, 25 px grid) and 2.2-2.6x (feet, eye, bill tip, 10 px grid), with raised contrast. Feet are tracked by continuity as footA and footB (near/far could not be assigned with confidence: both legs are lit in most frames). A foot is 'down' when its toes lie on the ground line of that frame (the planted foot's level); heel = the joint at the base of the toes (distal end of the tarsus). Head: billTip (sharp in every frame) and eye (readable in frames 1, 2, 6-12). Head motion relative to the planted foot: billTipAheadOfPlantedFootPx = billTip x - planted heel x in the same frame; since the planted foot is fixed on the ground, its change between frames is the head's ground speed, whatever the camera. Scale check across cameras: eye-to-bill-tip length 161-173 px (within +/-4%), and the bill angle (eye->tip) stays within 36-40 deg, so the bill tip stands in for the head. All points drawn back on the frames and checked. Adjutant faces right.
frameBoxesNote: Listed in time order, approximate to about 10 px. 3 rows of 4, numbered 1-12 left to right, top to bottom (handwritten numbers bottom left).

timing.cyclesSource: muybridge-1887-catalogue (fraction of a stride shown on the plate)
timing.observedComputed: footB lands between frames 3 and 4 and footA between 10 and 11: a step of 7 frames, so 14 frames per stride if both steps are equal; footA swings for 7 frames (up in 4-10) while footB stays down for at least 9 (4-12), which needs a stride of at least 16 frames if both feet swing equally long. Either way the plate shows 0.7-0.8 of a stride, more than the catalogue's 5/8. No time in seconds: the catalogue gives no interval for this plate.

findings: Walking stride about 14-16 frames; one step = 7 frames (landing to landing). The catalogue's 5/8 cycle (17.6 frames per stride) undercounts slightly: the plate shows 0.7-0.8 of a stride. No timing in seconds (no interval recorded).

Duty factor about 0.55 (0.50-0.62): footA's swing lasts 7 frames; footB is down in all of frames 4-12. Double support is brief or absent at one landing (frame 3->4) and at least 2 frames at the next (11-12): the walk is not quite symmetric on this plate, or the bird is slowing.

Clear hold-and-thrust head motion relative to the ground: during footB's stance the bill tip holds its ground position for 3 intervals (frames 6-9, while footA swings past), then thrusts forward 60-115 px per interval through footA's landing (frames 9-12); it also moved fast just after footB landed (frames 4-6, where the head is motion-blurred). The hold covers about 43% of each step. Head height above the foot stays constant (+/-5 px): the bob is horizontal only.

Compared with figures/goose.json walk (8 frames at 10 fps, duty 0.7, head hold 0.38, bob 1.2): the hold fraction (0.38) matches the adjutant (about 0.43). The goose's duty (0.7) is higher than the adjutant's 0.5-0.6, which is longer-legged with longer swings; the goose's vertical bob (1.2) has no counterpart in the adjutant's head, which stays level. Cycle length in time cannot be compared (no interval for this plate).

Not measured: near/far identity of the legs; leg joint angles (the intertarsal joints are partly hidden by the body and the feathered tibia); the toes of footB in frame 4; time in seconds; body bob (no clear body landmark).
